items.title: Replace misleading version-bump skip wording
items.context: DONE currently prints version bump skipped (no material code change). For experiment harness changes this is false; the real condition is no watched CLI/runtime inputs changed. Update the source constant and all dependent expectations.

happy.desc: DONE version-bump skip output for a non-runtime change says the skip happened because no watched CLI/runtime inputs changed, and the user-facing line no longer says no material code change; WHY: the wording matches the real runtime-scope condition.

edge.desc: All dependent expectations for the skip reason are updated consistently to the watched CLI/runtime inputs wording; WHY: no smoke snapshot or assertion preserves the old misleading phrase.

adversarial.desc: A focused negative check fails if the user-facing DONE/version-bump skip reason still contains no material code change anywhere in the exercised output path; WHY: a partial rename cannot leave the misleading phrase visible.

verificationEvidence.command: rg old/new skip phrase in version-bump.ts, version-bump-smoke.ts, story-lifecycle.md
verificationEvidence.note: Old user-facing skip phrase no material code change has no matches in the scoped source/smoke/docs, and VERSION_BUMP_SKIPPED_LINE now says version bump skipped (no watched CLI/runtime inputs changed).
version-bump smoke passed 68 assertions, including the updated skip-line expectation and existing patch-bump behavior.

verificationEvidence.command: ! rg -n "version bump skipped \(no material code change\)" packages/main/src/core/version-bump.ts packages/main/src/tasks/version-bump-smoke.ts docs/requirements/decisions/story-lifecycle.md
verificationEvidence.note: Focused negative check fails the story if the misleading no material code change phrase remains in the exercised skip-line path.

items.title: Prove DONE skip output distinguishes runtime scope from material code
items.context: Update focused smoke coverage so a non-runtime/material-code merge can skip CLI version bump with an accurate runtime-input explanation, while runtime-input changes still require build/bump behavior.

happy.desc: A focused smoke/test simulates or fixtures a non-runtime material-code change and observes a version-bump skip line that says no watched CLI/runtime inputs changed; WHY: non-runtime code can skip without misleading the user.

edge.desc: The same focused coverage proves a watched CLI/runtime input change still requires the build/version-bump path instead of the skip path; WHY: the wording change does not weaken the runtime gate.

adversarial.desc: The smoke/test would fail if the implementation merely rewrites prose while classifying runtime-scope changes incorrectly, including the old misleading phrase being gone and runtime-scope behavior remaining intact in one targeted run; WHY: text correctness and gate semantics must move together.

verificationEvidence.note: The smoke now proves the skip line for non-runtime/non-watched changes is phrased as no watched CLI/runtime inputs changed, matching the actual version policy boundary.
Existing version-bump assertions still prove watched CLI/runtime version sync files bump together; the wording change did not weaken runtime-input bump behavior.
TypeScript build passed and the targeted smoke passed, proving text correctness and version-bump semantics compile and run together.

items.title: Document the CLI-version boundary
items.context: Clarify that the CLI patch version tracks Proofbound CLI/runtime inputs, not every repository code artifact such as offline experiment harnesses; avoid changing product policy unless a later story introduces a separate experiment/product ledger.

happy.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/story-lifecycle.md explains that the CLI patch version tracks watched Proofbound CLI/runtime inputs, not every repository code artifact such as offline experiment harnesses; WHY: the version boundary is clear to future DONE operators.

edge.desc: The documentation preserves the existing rule that when watched CLI/runtime inputs change, the CLI patch version, package metadata or lockfile as applicable, build, and lattice --version verification are still required; WHY: the clarification cannot be read as a skip-all-code policy.

adversarial.desc: The documentation does not add experiments/** or offline experiment harnesses to the watched CLI/runtime policy and does not create a broader experiment/product ledger policy in this story; WHY: the fix clarifies the boundary without expanding scope.

verificationEvidence.command: rg -n "CLI patch version tracks watched Proofbound CLI/runtime inputs|not every repository code artifact" docs/requirements/decisions/story-lifecycle.md
verificationEvidence.note: story-lifecycle.md now explains that CLI patch versioning tracks watched Proofbound CLI/runtime inputs rather than every repository code artifact.
Documentation preserves the existing watched runtime input list and version/build verification duties for real CLI runtime changes.
Docs clarify that offline experiment harnesses are not automatically part of the CLI package version bump policy and do not introduce a new experiment/product ledger policy.
